beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:storyteller, low and inviting]On the walls of an Egyptian ^temple, priests carved a story. [act:storyteller, slow]An island in the first waters, its builder gods, and its ^destruction.
[d:tension][act:the hook, a raised eyebrow]Some say it's the ^oldest record@noun of ^Atlantis, the legendary lost island. [act:curious, fair][tune:rise]Is ^that what it is?

[d:calm][act:plain, setting the facts down]The Temple of Horus, the falcon god, at Edfu, beside the Nile in southern ^Egypt. [act:plain, precise]Begun in {237|^two thirty-seven} BCE and finished in {57|^fifty-seven} BCE: almost two ^centuries of work. [go:0|0][act:quiet admiration]Its walls hold one of the ^largest bodies of hieroglyphic text ^anywhere, like a library carved in ^stone.

[d:build][act:telling the myth, slow and rhythmic]The story goes like this. [act:same spell, unhurried]An ^island rises from the waters, covered in ^reeds. [act:same spell, unhurried]Creator beings ^gather. [act:a small image, gently]A ^falcon god ^lands on a reed.
[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:darker, then hope returns]^Enemies attack, the first gods ^die, and the world is made ^again.

[d:build][act:reporting the claim, even-handed]On a hugely popular podcast in {2026|twenty twenty-six}, a researcher reportedly called these texts the first records@noun of ^Atlantis, older than ^Plato. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]Plato is the Greek philosopher who first told the Atlantis ^story, around {360|three sixty} BCE.

[d:build][act:fair, giving it its due]And the writer Graham Hancock reads a sacred island destroyed by ^flood, whose wise men sailed away to ^rebuild the world. [act:the claim at its strongest][tune:rise]A real homeland, remembered as ^myth?

[d:reveal][sfx:hit][act:the turn, clear and deliberate][tune:fall]But first, the dates. [act:clear, deliberate]The stone was carved more than a century ^after Plato wrote. [act:building, a little wonder]And the island rising from the waters is Egypt's ^oldest creation image. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]It's already in the Pyramid Texts, spells carved inside pyramids around {2400|twenty-four hundred} BCE: two ^thousand years earlier.

[d:aside][act:gentle, an image to picture]Picture the land that told it. [act:gentle, explaining]Every summer the Nile ^flooded the valley. [act:gentle, wonder]And as the flood ^fell, the first mounds of dark, rich earth ^rose from the water, like ^islands.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]A memory of a ^lost civilisation? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Awaiting ^evidence*. [act:precise, unhurried]^Nothing in the texts points ^outside Egypt. [act:warmer, generous][tune:rise]Ideas ^older than the stone? [act:easy, confident]Very ^likely.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, gentle and clear]A ^creation story is not a ^travel report. [act:warm, a small smile]It can ^still be one of the ^oldest on any wall.
